trust_decision.summary: The lwIP wget receive callback decides whether the TCP/TLS connection is still alive after it rejects a block (buffer-size or LMB check fails). It calls altcp_abort(), which frees the pcb (and through the err callback the httpc state), but then returns ERR_BUF instead of ERR_ABRT. The caller (tcp_in.c, or altcp_tls_mbedtls.c for HTTPS) then treats the pcb or state as live and stores the already-freed pbuf as refused data.

landing_point.why: The summary names the lwIP wget receive callback, which is httpc_recv_cb, and its only error branch sits at net/lwip/wget.c:207-211.

fix_sites.entry_point: U-Boot shell command `wget` (cmd/lwip/wget.c:222), plus EFI HTTP boot (lib/efi_loader/efi_bootmgr.c:523) and EFI_HTTP_PROTOCOL via wget_request (lib/efi_loader/efi_net.c:1676)
fix_sites.module_kind: network application callback (lwIP HTTP client receive callback in U-Boot's lwIP glue)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The HTTPS path through lib/lwip/lwip/src/apps/altcp_tls/altcp_tls_mbedtls.c:352-365 reaches the same callback, and the same one-line change closes it. No separate site exists.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Removing altcp_abort() and keeping ERR_BUF looks like a fix, and a solver could argue that the vendored lwIP core/TLS code is third-party and out of scope. It is not a fix: with a non-OK return, lwIP expects the callee to keep the pbuf (tcp_in.c:512-518), so freeing it at wget.c:216 is still a double free.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: After the fix, failure reporting changes. httpc_result_cb suppresses the error message only for err == ERR_BUF, which is the headers_done oversize rejection that EFI HTTP relies on to re-request with a larger buffer. The abort path now arrives as ERR_ABRT through httpc_tcp_err. An over-broad fix that rewrites the err/ERR_BUF handling, or that makes headers_done abort as well, would break the EFI HTTP grow-buffer retry.

O6_input_shapes: body longer than wget_info->buffer_size (EFI HTTP sets buffer_size, net/lwip/wget.c:159)
body overlapping LMB-reserved memory or wrapping the address space when set_bootdev is set (net/lwip/wget.c:162-170)
plain HTTP (tcp_in.c refused_data route) and HTTPS (altcp_tls_mbedtls pass_rx_data route), both through the same callback

O8b_injection_room.sibling: headers_done callback that rejects an oversize Content-Length by calling altcp_abort() before returning an error, after which httpc_close/httpc_free_state reuses req->pcb
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer who wants the oversize case to fail fast would naturally copy the abort-on-error idiom from the recv callback 70 lines above.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second abort-then-continue branch in the recv callback (for example an HTTP status or Content-Length mismatch check) that frees the pbuf and returns a non-ABRT error
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The callback is the natural place for extra transfer validation, and the error-return contract is non-obvious (tcp.h:67-79).

O9_family: memory safety: use-after-free / double free from a callback return-code contract violation (CWE-416)

O10_build.toolchain: GNU make + gcc, Kconfig (sandbox defconfig with CONFIG_NET_LWIP and CMD_WGET)
services: HTTP server reachable from the sandbox ethernet (or an emulated peer) to drive the receive path
O10_build.project_tests: test/cmd/wget.c (unit test, built via test/cmd/Makefile:45 for CONFIG_CMD_WGET; appears to target the legacy net/wget.c stack); test/py/tests/test_efi_loader.py references wget. No lwIP-specific wget test for the abort path was found.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Drop the altcp_abort() call and keep returning ERR_BUF (or skip pbuf_free). This trades the UAF for a double free through refused_data, or for a stalled connection.

out_of_scope_notes: net/lwip/wget.c:373-377: on ctrl-C the loop breaks without closing the httpc connection, while callback_arg points at the stack ctx of wget_do_request (net/lwip/wget.c:391); this may be a separate dangling-callback issue, not pursued.
Legacy stack net/wget.c uses a different TCP implementation (net/tcp.c stream callbacks) with no abort/return-code contract; not a sibling of this mechanism.
